subject: Unexpected usage spike and overage on July invoice — request for credit
content:
From: Emma Ross <billing@brightcart.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Cc: platform@brightcart.com
Date: Sun, 15 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Unexpected July overage — request for review and credit

Hi Markus,

We just received the July invoice (attached) and there is a large overage line (~120k tokens) that doesn't match what our team observed. We ran a scheduled batch ingest on 2027-07-28 (internal test) that should have been scoped to our staging key, but the consumption appears to have been charged to our production namespace.

Can Redwood review the metering for the 07/28 window and advise whether this can be reclassified as non-billable or eligible for a one-time credit? I've attached the invoice and a small CSV with sample request IDs and timestamps (usage_snippet_20270815.csv) and a trimmed session trace (session-trace-logs-20270815.txt).

This overage would materially impact our monthly run rate and we're beginning renewal discussions in September — would appreciate a quick turnaround.

Thanks,
Emma Ross
Billing Operations | BrightCart
billing@brightcart.com

---
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Emma Ross <billing@brightcart.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Aug 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Unexpected July overage — request for review and credit

Hi Emma — thanks for the note and the attachments, forwarding to our infra and billing teams for an initial review. Two quick asks to help speed this up:

- Can you confirm the API key ID used for the batch run (prod vs staging)?
- Approximate time window for the ingest (you attached sample timestamps but a 10-min window helps).

Priyom: can you take a look at the sample trace and check for any signs of key attribution or unusual prefix caching that would explain a large token count? Grace: looping you in for billing/credit guidance.

I’ll follow up as soon as we have a preliminary root cause.

Thanks,
Markus Klein
Head of Sales Ops | Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwood.com

---
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Emma Ross <billing@brightcart.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Aug 2027 08:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Unexpected July overage — request for review and credit

Markus / Emma — I pulled the trimmed session trace. A few observations:

- The trace shows many short lived sessions with unusually large initial prompts (long concatenated payloads). If those were streamed as single requests they can multiply token counts due to prompt+response accounting.
- There is a key id in the headers (key_id: bc-prod-92) — can you confirm this is BrightCart's production key? If that matches their prod key, attribution is straightforward.
- We sometimes see replayed ingest jobs that re-send batched documents multiple times; if there was no dedupe at the client side each document can count multiple times.

Attached a short note on how we compute token attributions for batched streaming (sample_token_calc.txt). If BrightCart confirms the key was staging, we can scope this as a mis-attribution issue and look at a credit. If it was prod, policy is more restrictive but we can still evaluate goodwill credit given the renewal context.

— Priyom
Priyom Das
Infrastructure Reliability | Redwood Inference
priyom.das@redwood.com

Attachment: sample_token_calc.txt (explanatory note)

---
From: Emma Ross <billing@brightcart.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Cc: platform@brightcart.com
Date: Tue, 17 Aug 2027 11:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Unexpected July overage — request for review and credit

Thanks — confirmed: our DevOps accidentally used the production key for the replay job (key id bc-prod-92). That run occurred between 2027-07-28T02:10:00Z and 2027-07-28T02:35:00Z and included ~18k payloads with some larger-than-expected prompts. We've attached the fuller session IDs (in the CSV) and are happy to provide additional logs if you need them.

We understand production mistakes can generate billable traffic, but given this was an honest stager mistake and we're in renewal talks, is there any standard practice for a one-time mitigation or credit?

Emma
Emma Ross
Billing Operations | BrightCart

---
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Emma Ross <billing@brightcart.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Aug 2027 14:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Unexpected July overage — request for review and credit

Emma — appreciate the quick confirmation. Priyom: thanks for the early triage.

Operational position: because the traffic is tied to the production key (bc-prod-92) we cannot automatically mark the usage as non-billable without evidence it was run against a non-production namespace. That said, given BrightCart's long-standing usage and active renewal discussions, Sales/Billing are prepared to consider a one-time credit pending a short audit. Proposed next steps:

1) Infra (Priyom) to validate token-level traces and confirm whether the payloads show signs of replay/dedup opportunities (ETA 48 hours).
2) BrightCart to provide any internal CI/CD job ids or commit ids that link the run to a staging pipeline (helps our security/billing team).
3) Redwood Billing to provisionally prepare a credit memo (one-time, capped) while audit completes.

As a starting point, Redwood can provisionally propose a one-time 50% credit on the spike above their baseline for July, subject to audit confirmation. Ben — can you coordinate renewal sales impact if we move forward with this?

Regards,
Markus

---
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Emma Ross <billing@brightcart.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Aug 2027 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Unexpected July overage — request for review and credit

Hi Emma — following up with next steps and an interim decision from Redwood: we completed an initial audit of the provided session traces and confirmed that the bulk of the spike aligns with repeated batched payloads originating from the key you indicated. The traffic pattern strongly suggests a CI replay from a non-idempotent job.

Given the context (renewal, first large mistake of this nature, and prompt cooperation), Redwood is prepared to issue a one-time, retrospective credit for 70% of the spike amount above BrightCart's historical baseline for July 2027. This credit is limited to the spike and is conditional on BrightCart providing the internal CI run id and a short signed statement acknowledging the mistaken key usage for our records.

I've attached a draft credit memo (approved-credit-memo-draft.pdf) — once we receive the CI job id and the signed note we will apply the credit to your next invoice.

If that works, please reply with the CI id and I'll loop finance to apply the credit. Happy to hop on a call if you prefer.

Best,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
